Title: Onboard a new merchant via portal endpoint - the full flow now executes instead of returning null
Preconditions: A valid merchant portal onboarding request exists with merchant name, mobile number, email, business type, and store location; the KYC service endpoint is reachable and the merchant service is available
Steps:
1. Submit the portal onboarding request with merchant details. 2. The system registers the user via the KYC service. 3. The system submits KYC for the registered user. 4. The system creates a merchant account using the registered user ID. 5. The response is returned.

Test Data: Merchant name: 'Test Merchant', mobile number: '01712345678', email: 'merchant@example.com', business type: 'RETAIL', store location: 'Dhaka, Bangladesh'
Expected Result: HTTP status 201 CREATED is returned with a response body containing the merchant name and the created merchant object including account number and merchant ID; the user is registered, KYC is submitted, and the merchant account is created

Title: Submit KYC information for a registered user and receive a confirmation
Preconditions: A user has been registered and has a valid user ID; KYC data including name, national ID, and KYC step are available
Steps:
1. Prepare KYC submission data with the user ID, name, national ID, and KYC step. 2. Submit the KYC information to the KYC service. 3. Receive the response.

Test Data: User ID: 1001, name: 'John Doe', national ID: '1234567890123', KYC step: 'COMPLETE'
Expected Result: KYC data is saved successfully and the response indicates success with a KYC record ID and KYC status

Title: Mobile number shorter than 4 characters is fully masked
Preconditions: A merchant portal onboarding attempt is made, and the MmsUtils.maskMobileNumber utility is invoked for log output when a mobile number is logged.
Steps:
1. Trigger a portal onboarding request with a mobile number of fewer than 4 characters (e.g. '12'). 2. Observe the log line that records the mobile number.

Test Data: Mobile number: '12' (length 2, well below the 4-character threshold)
Expected Result: The log line shows the mobile number rendered as '****' (four asterisks), revealing no digits of the original value.

Title: Exactly 4-character mobile number is masked except the last digit
Preconditions: The MmsUtils.maskMobileNumber utility is exercised through any logging path that prints the merchant's mobile number.
Steps:
1. Submit a request that causes the mobile number to be logged. 2. Use a mobile number of exactly 4 characters. 3. Inspect the log entry that contains the masked number.

Test Data: Mobile number: '1234' (length 4, exactly at the lower threshold that the code treats as 'too short to partially show')
Expected Result: The log entry shows '****' (four asterisks), NOT '******1234' - because the code's early-return condition is 'length < 4', a 4-character number still falls into the fully-masked branch.

Title: 5-character mobile number exposes exactly its last 4 digits
Preconditions: A portal onboarding flow is run that logs the merchant's mobile number via MmsUtils.maskMobileNumber.
Steps:
1. Submit a request with a 5-character mobile number. 2. Locate the log line containing the masked mobile number. 3. Compare the visible suffix to the original value.

Test Data: Mobile number: '12345' (length 5, the first length where the normal masking branch runs)
Expected Result: The log shows '******2345' - six asterisks followed by the last 4 digits of the original number, regardless of how short the original is.

Title: Standard-length mobile number reveals only the last 4 digits
Preconditions: A portal onboarding submission is made and the log line for the merchant's mobile number is captured.
Steps:
1. Submit a portal onboarding request with a normal-length mobile number. 2. Inspect the log entry that prints the mobile number via the masking utility.

Test Data: Mobile number: '01712345678' (length 11, a typical Bangladeshi mobile number length)
Expected Result: The log shows '******5678' - exactly 6 asterisks then the last 4 digits; the first 7 digits are never visible.

Title: Null mobile number passed to the masker does not throw
Preconditions: A portal onboarding request is made where the mobile number field is absent or null, and the code path that logs the mobile number via MmsUtils.maskMobileNumber is reached.
Steps:
1. Submit a portal onboarding request with the mobile number field left empty / null. 2. Check that the log line containing the masked mobile number is produced without an error. 3. Read the masked value in the log.

Test Data: Mobile number: null (field omitted from the request)
Expected Result: No exception is raised; the log line shows the literal string '****' for the mobile-number portion (the utility returns its null input unchanged, and the caller renders this as a 4-asterisk placeholder in the log).

Title: Prefix plus suffix length equal to the string length returns the string unchanged
Section: MmsUtils mask - boundary behavior on prefix/suffix sum
Preconditions: Any code path that invokes the general mask(accountNo, prefixLength, suffixLength) helper with values that stress the boundary is exercised.
Steps:
1. Invoke the masking helper with an input string and a prefix length + suffix length that exactly equals the string length. 2. Read the returned value. 3. Compare it to the input.

Test Data: Input string: 'ABCDE' (5 characters); prefixLength = 3; suffixLength = 2 (3 + 2 = 5, equal to the string length)
Expected Result: The helper returns the input string 'ABCDE' with no asterisks inserted, because the early-return condition triggers when prefix + suffix is greater than or equal to the string length.

Title: Prefix plus suffix one less than the string length produces a single asterisk
Section: MmsUtils mask - boundary behavior on prefix/suffix sum
Preconditions: The general mask helper is invoked with parameters chosen to fall just inside its normal masking branch.
Steps:
1. Invoke the masking helper with an input string where prefix length + suffix length is one less than the total length. 2. Read the returned value. 3. Count the asterisks.

Test Data: Input string: 'ABCDE' (5 characters); prefixLength = 2; suffixLength = 2 (2 + 2 = 4, one less than 5)
Expected Result: The helper returns 'AB*DE' - exactly 1 asterisk between the first 2 and the last 2 characters.

Title: Negative prefix length is rejected with an error
Section: MmsUtils mask - boundary behavior on negative lengths
Preconditions: Any code path that calls the general mask helper is available, and the boundary condition is hit by passing a negative prefix length.
Steps:
1. Invoke the masking helper with a negative prefix length. 2. Observe the outcome of the call.

Test Data: Input string: 'ABCDE' (5 characters); prefixLength = -1; suffixLength = 2
Expected Result: The helper throws an IllegalArgumentException (visible to the caller as a clear error) - it does not return a silently corrupted masked value.

Title: Negative suffix length is rejected with an error
Section: MmsUtils mask - boundary behavior on negative lengths
Preconditions: The general mask helper is invoked with a negative suffix length value.
Steps:
1. Invoke the masking helper with a negative suffix length. 2. Observe the outcome.

Test Data: Input string: 'ABCDE' (5 characters); prefixLength = 1; suffixLength = -1
Expected Result: The helper throws an IllegalArgumentException, refusing the request rather than returning a string with a negative-position substring.

Title: Null or blank input is returned unchanged by the general mask helper
Section: MmsUtils mask - boundary behavior on empty / null input
Preconditions: The general mask helper is invoked with a null or whitespace-only input.
Steps:
1. Invoke the masking helper with a null input. 2. Observe the returned value. 3. Repeat with a blank/whitespace-only input.

Test Data: Input string: null (first call) and '   ' (second call, all whitespace); prefixLength = 1; suffixLength = 1
Expected Result: The helper returns the null reference unchanged for the first call, and the whitespace string unchanged for the second call - no exception, no asterisks inserted.
